chunks: Sa'd narrated from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Ibrahim al-Aws al-Awsy, from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard my father saying: 'One day I was with my father when a man came to him and said, I am a man from Ahl al-Ray and I have zakat, to whom should I give it?' He said, 'To us.' He said, 'Is not charity (sadaqah) forbidden for you?' He said, 'Yes, if you give it to our shi'ah, you have given it to us.' He said, 'I do not know anyone for it.' He said, 'Wait with it for one year.' He said, 'If I do not find anyone for it?' He said, 'Wait with it for two years, until it reaches four years.' Then he said to him, 'If you do not find anyone for it, then shake it out vigorously and throw it into the sea, for indeed Allah, Exalted and Majestic, has forbidden our wealth and the wealth of our shi'ah upon our enemy.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on giving zakat to the Imams and what happens if no recipient is found?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida clarifies the distinction between general charity (sadaqah) and obligatory alms (zakat), establishing that while the Imams are forbidden from receiving sadaqah, they are eligible recipients of zakat through their faithful followers (shi'ah). The detailed instruction to retain the funds for up to four years before discarding them in the sea highlights the high status of the Imams' wealth and the specific condition that their wealth is forbidden for their enemies, a concept rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding the purity of their assets.
